purpose: Document city-scope registry evidence and bounded public parcel-geometry route review.
assessment: The city cadastral office and municipality map services are verified. The municipality’s E-İmar page exposes parcel/address selectors, while TKGM’s static client supports coordinate-based parcel lookup; without a documented geometry/ID-only response allowlist, no feature query was sent.
registryAssessment: TKGM’s official directory lists Şanlıurfa Kadastro Müdürlüğü in Haliliye. Şanlıurfa Metropolitan Municipality links a Kent Rehberi and E-İmar service from its official homepage. These are local cadastral and city-planning sources; no geometry-only parcel schema was verified.

officialPrimarySources.observation: TKGM’s official directory lists Şanlıurfa Kadastro Müdürlüğü in Haliliye. Şanlıurfa Metropolitan Municipality links a Kent Rehberi and E-İmar service from its official homepage. These are local cadastral and city-planning sources; no geometry-only parcel schema was verified.

The official city homepage links Kent Rehberi and E-İmar. An anonymous GET of the KEOS map shell returned HTTP 200 and its public HTML initializes a Netcad map workspace; the visible startup config does not disclose a safe parcel-feature schema. The E-İmar page displays district, neighborhood, street, door-number and ada/parsel selectors and was not submitted. TKGM’s new `parselsorguv2` hostname failed direct DNS resolution (curl exit 6; no HTTP response); its legacy public shell returned HTTP 200 and its static client exposes a coordinate-query route. The published static client does not provide a verified safe field allowlist for geometry retrieval, so no parcel feature request was made. These failures are transport/schema holds, not proof of absent parcel data.
